title: The Victorian with Too Many Windows
premise: A building adds one window whenever a secret is spoken nearby.
pressure: An Old Town Victorian grows an extra window whenever a pedestrian admits a secret. Its owner is selling tickets to the confession tour.
investigate: Count windows while asking about the building's permits
success: The newly grown sash frames a room whose wallpaper shows the harbor ten years from now.
failure: The window disappears before the camera focuses; its reflection stays in a shop across the street.
help: Help a resident stop the invasive tours
helpOutcome: The building closes its last extra window and the neighbor can sleep without being watched.

title: Antique Shop of Almost-Famous Objects
premise: The shop sells history's second-best cursed relics at honest prices.
pressure: The antique shop sells second-place relics: the pen almost used to sign a treaty and the hat a famous ghost chose not to wear.
investigate: Verify a relic's history before it leaves the shop
success: The object is ordinary but its label predicts a municipal vote still weeks away.
failure: You buy an impressive fake; the shopkeeper refunds you after you explain why attribution matters.
help: Help the clerk return a misidentified family keepsake
helpOutcome: A grandmother recovers her box, which is more valuable than any curse.

title: A Ghost Demands Parking Validation
premise: An Edwardian apparition refuses to haunt without reimbursed meter fees.
pressure: An Edwardian ghost refuses to haunt until his parking meter is validated. The council wants to tow the only car anyone can see through.
investigate: Check the ghost's citation against archived street maps
success: His ticket names a vanished lane and a courthouse hearing scheduled tomorrow.
failure: The ticket crumbles, but the ghost remembers the clerk who issued it.
help: Advocate for accessible public parking, living and otherwise
helpOutcome: The meter attendant offers a sensible pass and the apparition finally moves his cart.

title: The Postcard from Eureka, Mars
premise: A tourist card shows an accurate street scene under two suns.
pressure: A postcard under two suns depicts Eureka's same waterfront with a transit line that doesn't exist. The tourist says the souvenir was cheap on Mars.
success: The shadows point to a building that is present today but absent on every printed map.
failure: Rain blurs the address; the second sun remains a clean bright ring on the varnish.
help: Share the impossible card with a local archive
helpOutcome: A conservator protects the paper and allows residents to annotate what looks wrong.

title: The Perilous Plunge into Monday
premise: A costumed jumper emerges from Humboldt Bay on a different day.
place: Eureka F Street waterfront / Perilous Plunge
pressure: A costumed bay jumper surfaces on Monday after entering on Saturday. Her friends insist the clock is only ten seconds ahead.
investigate: Correlate her wristwatch with harbor announcements
success: The watch recorded a weather warning two days before the microphones broadcast it.
failure: The watch stops when you touch it, but her soggy race bib bears Monday's date.
help: Get the chilled jumper warm before any interview
helpOutcome: The rescue volunteers make a plan that values a person over a spectacular headline.

title: The Judge Who Is Also an Octopus
premise: A fundraiser award panel has an unusually flexible member.
place: Eureka F Street waterfront / Perilous Plunge
pressure: The award judge is an octopus in borrowed robes. Every arm holds a different scorecard and none agrees about the rules.
success: Four arms point to four versions of the same entry that cannot all have been built.
failure: Ink covers the table, but a volunteer saves one perfectly legible dissent.
help: Let the teams argue for fair criteria
helpOutcome: The octopus awards a shared prize for ingenuity and lets the losers keep their pride.

title: Best Costume: Unidentified Object
premise: Someone registers as a weather balloon with very convincing paperwork.
place: Eureka F Street waterfront / Perilous Plunge
pressure: A contestant dressed as a weather balloon has filed forms declaring it an unidentified object. Inspectors find the paperwork alarmingly convincing.
investigate: Trace the registration number without detaining the performer
success: Its serial number belongs to a weather station reporting from a future drought.
failure: The permit says CLASSIFIED and the wind steals it before you can copy the code.
help: Defend the contestant's right to compete anonymously
helpOutcome: Judges award the costume a place without requiring anyone to surrender their name.

title: The Marching Lumberjack Paradox
premise: A drumbeat repeats yesterday's parade in reverse.
place: Eureka F Street waterfront / Perilous Plunge
pressure: A drumline passes backward along F Street while everyone else walks forward. The tune remembers a parade that has not happened yet.
investigate: Record the cadence and map each backward step
success: The drumbeat encodes a street closure required by tomorrow's impossible tide.
failure: Your recorder catches only applause; the drummer writes the odd rhythm on your hand.
help: Guide the crowd away from the collision
helpOutcome: Marchers make space for pedestrians and the lost minute passes without injury.

title: The Hot Tub Oracle
premise: A post-plunge hot tub provides dubious prophecies in bubbles.
place: Eureka F Street waterfront / Perilous Plunge
pressure: The fundraiser's post-plunge hot tub speaks in bubbles, offering prophecies that are consistently useful and consistently wrong about who deserves credit.
investigate: Test one prediction against a public event
success: A bubble maps an upcoming ferry route but assigns it to someone who never sailed.
failure: The water turns cloudy, leaving you with a plausible warning and no author.
help: Ask the volunteers who actually kept everyone safe
helpOutcome: The prophecy stops talking long enough for the crew to receive a thank-you.

title: The Oyster Council Convenes
premise: A floating shellfish parliament has issued a subpoena for a gull.
pressure: Oysters convene a floating parliament and subpoena a gull for stealing mussels. The gull's defense is that the tide taught it to.
success: The shell minutes reveal a channel marker missing from the next day's chart.
failure: The gull swallows the notice, but two witnesses agree on the location.
helpOutcome: The council reserves a feeding patch and the gull promises only to steal human french fries.

title: The Missing Channel Marker
premise: A navigational buoy goes on strike because the sea keeps lying.
pressure: A channel buoy has walked off its station and announced a strike. It says the sea keeps giving false directions.
investigate: Measure the vacancy with a passing skipper
success: The buoy's old position is correct on a chart dated next year, not today's.
failure: Your compass spins and the buoy refuses another shift until someone listens.
help: Help boaters place an honest temporary marker
helpOutcome: Crews post a clear warning and agree to investigate instead of blaming the buoy.

title: Submarine with Bicycle Pedals
premise: A homemade contraption claims to be a federally funded research craft.
pressure: A pedal-driven submarine claims a federal research grant, but its crew are three tired mechanics and a child holding a clipboard.
investigate: Review the grant documentation and hull design
success: The sponsor is a department that will be founded after the next great storm.
failure: The submarine leaks before the test; the mechanics record the flaw in good faith.
helpOutcome: Visitors enjoy the invention without sending the child below the waterline.

title: The Tide Returns a Bicycle
premise: A rustless bike carries evidence of a trip nobody remembers.
pressure: The tide deposits a rustless bicycle with fresh sand in its gears. A rental sticker names a journey none of the staff remembers.
investigate: Check the frame number with the ferry records
success: It was checked out tomorrow by a rider who crossed the bay through the missing channel.
failure: Salt takes the ink off the sticker, but the wheels turn backward once without contact.
help: Return the bicycle to the people who need it
helpOutcome: A youth cycling group repairs the brakes and makes its mystery public.

title: The Redwood's Lost-and-Found
premise: A park bench collects small things that people forgot as children.
pressure: A park bench has gathered objects visitors forgot as children, including one nobody can bear to identify. A caretaker wants the bench removed.
investigate: Find the oldest returned object and ask who remembers it
success: A toy compass points to the tree with three doorways rather than magnetic north.
failure: You recognize a toy but not its owner; the bench offers no explanation.
help: Help people reclaim memories without performing grief
helpOutcome: Visitors leave messages for one another. The bench keeps only what they choose to donate.

title: The Volunteer in the Bear Costume
premise: The person giving animal talks cannot take off their costume.
pressure: A volunteer inside a bear suit delivers exact animal facts, then admits the zipper has been missing for months. The bear now corrects him when he lies.
investigate: Inspect the costume seam without frightening the volunteer
success: The inner lining bears a zoo inventory label written in a future handwriting.
failure: The zipper breaks again; the volunteer laughs despite exhaustion.
help: Arrange a break and a humane solution
helpOutcome: A seamstress sews in a new opening while the bear politely looks away.

title: A Peacock with a Search Warrant
premise: An extremely official bird investigates missing color.
pressure: An official-looking peacock investigates stolen pigments at the zoo. His search warrant describes a color no human visitor can see, and several painted signs have gone white.
investigate: Read the warrant and inspect the stripped murals
success: The missing pigment glitters on a dated transfer slip for a future conservation exhibit; the peacock's case is real to him.
failure: The bird confiscates your pencil, but a keeper confirms the paint vanished before the search began.
help: Help the keepers restore the public signs without frightening animals
helpOutcome: Visitors work from remembered colors; the peacock leaves his badge with the staff as a thank-you.

title: The Picnic That Never Ends
premise: One family has been packing up the same picnic for decades.
pressure: One family has spent decades finishing the same picnic. Each time they fold the cloth, another child arrives at the table.
investigate: Compare the photographs around the basket
success: The youngest child's birthday lies thirty years in the future, yet the cake is fresh.
failure: The album closes before you copy a date; the family still invites you to sit.
help: Help them decide when a gathering may end
helpOutcome: The parents pack at last and carry the leftovers to the shelter rather than hold the children forever.

title: The Tree That Grows Entrances
premise: A hollow trunk offers three doors, none requiring a key.
pressure: A hollow redwood holds three doorways: PUBLIC, PRIVATE and FORGOTTEN. A ranger says none has a key and all have an exit.
investigate: Test each threshold from outside with a witness
success: The public doorway opens onto a future trail meeting, including its still-blank sign-in sheet.
failure: The forgotten door seals when named; you chalk its outline for a safer return.
help: Ask who should decide access to the tree
helpOutcome: Local stewards agree to survey the site before turning the anomaly into a tourist attraction.
